h1: The 5 Best Electric Pruning Shears With Two Batteries of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Two-Battery Pruning Shears: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 5 best electric pruning shears that ship with two batteries, compared on cutting diameter, runtime and spare blades.
summary: The ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch is the best electric pruning shear with two batteries: the widest stated cut, two packs and spare blades. The 2.56 inch sibling gives up little and costs less. The KOMOK 1.65 inch is the pick when a published 8 to 10 hour runtime matters, while the Upgraded shears are the cheapest brushless two-battery kit for light work.
intro: Most buyers count batteries and forget the one number that decides whether the tool is useful: cutting diameter. Two packs double your working time, but if the jaws top out at 1.2 inches you will reach for a handsaw the moment you meet a thick branch. Capacity is what separates a real pruner from a rose trimmer with a battery.

We kept only models whose listings state two included batteries and ranked them by cutting diameter, stated runtime, spare blades and extras such as a brushless motor or LCD. These are paper rankings from listing data, so verify the cut capacity against your thickest branch before ordering, and leave a margin, because stalled jaws cost you blades and batteries, so respect the ceiling.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.75'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: The largest cutting diameter here, with two batteries and spare blades in the box.
products.description:
The ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch has the widest stated cutting diameter in this ranking, with two batteries and spare blades included. Cut capacity is the spec that decides whether a pruner replaces a lopper or just supplements it. At 2.75 inches the jaws handle fruit-tree limbs and overgrown shrubs that smaller electric shears would stall on.

It takes first because it beats every rival on that number while still bundling the spares, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Against the KOMOK pair, its weak point is that the listing gives no stated runtime figure, so you are trusting the two packs.

Buy it for thick branches and regular heavy pruning. The caveat is bulk: a tool built for 2.75 inch cuts is heavier in the hand than a rose pruner, so skip it if you only trim small stems.
products.skipIf: You need a stated runtime figure.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.56'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: Nearly the same kit with a 2.56 inch cut.
products.description:
This ANTTCTIG variant cuts up to 2.56 inches and includes two batteries and spare blades, sharing the $50 to $100 bucket with the top pick. The cutting range is still wider than any non-ANTTCTIG model here, and the jaw-to-branch ratio is what protects the motor from stalling.

It ranks second because it gives up only about 0.19 inches of capacity compared with the 2.75 inch version, which rarely matters in practice. The listing positions it as the lower-priced option of the pair. Against the 1.65 inch KOMOK, you gain nearly an inch of cut.

Buy it if you want the same kit for a bit less. Skip it if every extra fraction of an inch counts. The caveat is the same as its sibling's: no stated runtime, so you cannot compare battery life with the KOMOK models.
pros: Lower cost than the top pick
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the ANTTCTIG kit for less.
products.skipIf: You need the maximum cutting capacity.

products.name: KOMOK Electric Pruning Shears, Professional Cordless Electric Pruners, 1.65" (42mm) Cutting Diameter
products.verdict: A named 8 to 10 hour runtime with two 2Ah batteries.
products.description:
The KOMOK 1.65 inch (42mm) comes with two 2Ah batteries and a stated runtime of 8 to 10 hours, the only published figure in this ranking worth comparing. A published number lets you plan a full orchard day instead of guessing. The 2Ah rating tells you each pack is small, so two of them are what make the claim plausible.

It ranks third because a 1.65 inch cut is well under the ANTTCTIG pair, and it costs more, in the $100 to $200 bucket. What you get in exchange is a concrete runtime, which neither ANTTCTIG listing offers.

Buy it for long pruning sessions where runtime matters. The caveat is capacity: skip it if you cut thick limbs, because 42mm is the ceiling and stalled cuts will wear the blades.
products.idealFor: Long pruning sessions where runtime matters.

products.name: Upgraded Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Diameter Cordless Pruner with LCD Display, Brushless Motor, 2x2.0Ah Batteries & Extra Blade
products.verdict: Two batteries, an extra blade, a brushless motor and an LCD at the lowest cost.
products.description:
These Upgraded shears cut up to 1.4 inches and include two 2.0Ah batteries, an extra blade, a brushless motor and an LCD display. Brushless motors run cooler and waste less power than brushed ones, which matters when both packs are small. An LCD shows battery state so you do not discover a dead pack mid-cut. This is the cheapest kit, in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks fourth because the cut is smaller than the ANTTCTIG pair, but the feature list is stronger than the price implies. A brushless motor plus an LCD is unusual at this level.

Buy it for light garden work on a budget. The caveat is capacity and name: skip it above 1.5 inches, and treat the unfamiliar brand as a risk for parts and service.
products.idealFor: Light pruning for the least money.

products.name: KOMOK Electric Pruning Shears, Cordless Electric Pruner Battery Operated Tree Branch Cutter, 1.2 inch (30mm) Cutting Diameter
products.verdict: The same stated runtime with a smaller 1.2 inch cut.
products.description:
The KOMOK 1.2 inch (30mm) includes two 2Ah batteries and the same stated 8 to 10 hour runtime as its bigger sibling, in the $100 to $200 bucket. The smaller jaw is a deliberate fit for roses, fruit trees and light shrubs, where a lighter tool is less tiring over hours of repetitive cuts.

It ranks last because its cut is the smallest here, while the price bucket matches the 1.65 inch KOMOK. The cheaper Upgraded shears also give you a 1.4 inch cut for less, with a brushless motor and an LCD, which this model lacks.

Buy it for delicate, high-volume pruning. The caveat is value. Skip it if you want more capacity per dollar, because both the Upgraded and ANTTCTIG kits cost less and cut thicker.
pros: Suited to roses and fruit trees
products.skipIf: You want more cutting capacity per dollar.

whatMatters.detail: Cutting diameter is the thickest branch the jaws can close on, and it ranges from 1.2 to 2.75 inches here. A tool rated below your thickest branch will stall or jam, wearing blades and motors. Check the exact inch or millimeter figure in the title, and leave margin below the rating for dense or dead wood. Measure the branch with calipers or a tape.

Capacity is measured in amp-hours, and a 2Ah pack holds less energy than a larger one. Two packs mean you swap rather than stop to charge, which is the real benefit of this category. Look for the Ah rating of each pack in the listing, since a bare two batteries line tells you nothing about size. Bigger packs also add weight at the grip.

Runtime is how long a charge lasts under light work, and most listings leave it out. The KOMOK models state 8 to 10 hours, which is a genuine comparison point. If the listing gives no figure, as the ANTTCTIG pair does not, treat the battery as an unknown and plan to charge between sessions. Cold weather tends to shorten any battery runtime.

Blades dull and nick, especially on dirty or woody cuts, and dull blades crush stems rather than slice them, which damages the plant. A listing that bundles spares saves a separate purchase. Check the contents list for the number of extra blades, as on the ANTTCTIG shears, and confirm replacements remain available later.

A brushless motor typically runs cooler and wastes less power than a brushed one, which stretches small batteries between charges. It is a useful extra, not a substitute for cutting capacity. Look for the word brushless in the specs, as the Upgraded shears list, and for an LCD that shows the charge state.

faq.q: Do the batteries fit other tools?
faq.a: The listings do not say, so assume the packs are specific to each pruner. Check the product page for compatibility before buying spares, especially for the ANTTCTIG and KOMOK shears, and avoid mixing packs between brands.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing by battery count alone. Two batteries mean nothing if the cutting diameter is below your thickest branch. The KOMOK 1.2 inch has two packs but the smallest cut in the guide at 30mm.

faq.q: Is the ANTTCTIG worth it over the Upgraded shears?
faq.a: If you cut branches thicker than 1.4 inches, yes. The 2.75 inch ANTTCTIG gives much more capacity, while the Upgraded shears suit light work and cost less, in the $25 to $50 bucket, though they stop short of thicker limbs.

faq.q: How do I start using electric shears?
faq.a: Charge both batteries, fit one, and test a cut on a thin branch. Keep the blade clean and sharp for consistent cuts, and swap packs before the first one fully drains to avoid stalling mid-cut.

faq.q: Do I need to replace the blades?
faq.a: Eventually, yes. The ANTTCTIG listings include spare blades, and the Upgraded shears include one extra blade. The KOMOK models list none, so budget for replacements if you buy one of them, and keep the old blade for dead wood.
Dead wood is harder on blades, so use a model with spare blades, like the ANTTCTIG, and stay under the stated cutting diameter. Hard, dry stems dull jaws faster than green growth does.

finalTake: For most gardeners, the ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch is the right electric pruner: the widest cut, two batteries and spare blades. The 2.56 inch sibling saves money for a fraction less capacity. Pick the KOMOK 1.65 inch if a published runtime is a firm requirement, and the Upgraded shears for light work on a budget. Always match the cut capacity to your thickest branch.
